Programme Outline

Awarded and developed by: University of Alberta, Canada


With a 100-year legacy as one of Canada's top business schools, the University of Alberta Bachelor of Commerce (BCom) program has empowered thousands of undergrads to shape their futures and become leaders in Alberta and around the world. 

The program aims to provide students with a well-rounded and diverse business education. Students learn how businesses and organizations work in areas such as 

  • Accounting & Finance
  • Marketing
  • Operations & Supply Chain
  • Human Resources & Leadership, and
  • Strategy & Entrepreneurship.

They will learn broad foundational knowledge and soft skills that are transferable and valued by employers.

Learning Outcomes

The learning outcomes of our BCom graduates are built on two equally important pillars.

Students develop a broad range of technical skills, including:

  • Financial analysis and budgeting
  • Data literacy, analytics, and decision-making tools
  • Market research and business planning
  • International business and supply chain management
  • Understanding of emerging technologies in business, including AI, digital platforms, and supply chain technologies

In addition, the program places strong emphasis on developing essential professional skills, including:

  • Written, verbal, and presentation communication
  • Teamwork and collaboration
  • Leadership and negotiation
  • Problem-solving and critical thinking
  • Cross-cultural awareness, essential for success in global business environments
  • Ethical decision-making, including an understanding of business ethics and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) principles and requirements

Further Studies & Career Prospects

Career Prospects

The University of Alberta BCom program prepares graduates for entry-level opportunities across a wide range of industries and business functions. These include:

  • Business analyst and management roles
  • Marketing professional
  • Financial analyst and banking specialist
  • Operations and supply chain roles
  • Human resources specialist and talent management roles
  • Sales, consulting, and customer success roles
  • Entrepreneurship and family business management

Opportunities for Further Study

As an internationally recognized degree, the University of Alberta BCom degree can also serve as a foundation for further graduate studies, and professional degrees and designations such as MBA, CPA, CFA, HR designations, and PMP.

Curriculum

Structure

This program will be delivered via a blended mode with face-to-face intensive teaching modules and online Components. 

The module “capstone project” is delivered via online learning. All modules are supported by academic and professional support staff and will combine a mix of guided study, independent study, online discussions, group, and individual activities.

Lecturers: UofA faculty and SIM local lecturers
Average teacher-student ratio: 1:30
Exemptions: Nil

Assessment & Attendance

All modules are assessed using a variety of methods including written assignments, exams, written reports, presentations, research proposals, case studies and online discussions. Formative assessments (plans or drafts) may be submitted at specified times during each module for feedback.  

Attendance requirement:
•    Local students – 75%
•    International students – 90%

Requirements to Graduate

SIM Diploma in Accounting/ Banking and Finance/ International Business/ Management Studies holders are eligible for up to 42 course equivalency credits, or 14- courses exemption. They will need to complete 26 courses (78 credits) in SIM. Courses to be completed in SIM depend on the transfer credits that are awarded in accordance with the Diploma that the students hold.

20 core and 11 electives, making a total of 31 courses will be offered in SIM. This will allow students to take all the required courses to graduate with the BCom degree in SIM.

Admission Criteria

Accepted Entry Qualifications

  • SIM Diploma in Accounting/ Banking and Finance/ International Business/ Management Studies; or
  • All other qualifications will be evaluated on a case-by-case basis

Applicants must obtain an average Grade B and may be required for interview before admission.
 

English Language Requirements

•    Possession of a degree or its academic equivalent from an institution recognized by the University of Alberta and where the language of instruction is English 

•    Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL iBT, in-person or special at-home edition) - Total score of 90 with a score of at least 21 on each of the individual skill areas (internet based) or equivalent.

•    Academic International English Language Testing System (IELTS)
    6.5, with at least 6.0 on each test band.

•    Pearson Test of English Academic (PTE Academic) -61 with a minimum band score of 60.

•    Equivalent.

Fees & Financial Aid

Programme fees are charged based on the number of credits taken during the semester.

Semester programme fees are payable prior to commencement of semester. Each semester typically has 6 to 7 modules (18 to 24 credits).
